title: Split semisimple simply connected group-scheme terminology over a ring
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, and $G$ a group object over $\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-sc-group-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For each algebraically closed field $F$ equipped with $R\to F$, let $G_F$ be the actual pullback group object. For a semisimple group $D$ over $F$ [def-sfb-semisimple-group-scheme], simple connectedness means that every surjective homomorphism $E\to D$ from a semisimple $F$-group with finite central kernel is an isomorphism; centrality is tested on all commutative $F$-algebra points. Define $G$ to be split semisimple simply connected if every $G_F$ is semisimple and simply connected, and there exist group objects $T,B$ over $R$ with closed group inclusions $i:T\to G$, $j:B\to G$ and a homomorphism $k:T\to B$ with $j\circ k=i$, such that $T$ is isomorphic to $\mathbf G_{m,R}^r$ for some $r\ge0$ [def-sfb-split-torus-over-ring], and on every geometric fibre $i_F$ is a maximal torus inclusion [def-sfb-reductive-torus-centralizer-terminology] and $j_F$ is a Borel subgroup inclusion [def-sfb-borel-subgroup-scheme]. This is a predicate only; it makes no choice of the pair, and includes rank zero. Smoothness, affineness and finite presentation of $G/R$, when needed, are stated separately.

source.place: Section 9.7, Lemmas 9.7.2 and 9.7.4 and Theorem 9.7.5, printed pp.526--528; primary PDF https://content.algebraicgeometry.nl/2014-4/2014-4-022.pdf
